inline_comments.comment: The condition `!maxPresetColors || maxPresetColors === Infinity` relies on the falsy check `!maxPresetColors` to detect the value `0`, which is non-obvious and also silently catches `NaN` (since `!NaN` is `true`). While `slice(-NaN)` happens to return all elements (NaN coerces to 0), this is accidental behavior. Prefer the explicit form `maxPresetColors === 0 || maxPresetColors === Infinity` so the two intended sentinel values are immediately self-documenting and NaN falls through to a predictable path.

The `WithMaxPresetColors` story has no `play` function. Per the project's testing convention, stories for interactive components (here, a color-picker popover) should include a `play` function that opens the picker so the non-default/open state is captured in visual regression runs. At minimum, click the color swatch to open the popover so the truncated preset list is actually visible in the snapshot.

Same issue as `WithMaxPresetColors`: `WithUnlimitedPresetColors` is missing a `play` function. Without opening the picker, the story only captures the collapsed swatch, making it ineffective as a visual regression test for the 40-color unlimited preset list.

general_comments.comment: No unit or integration tests are added for the new `maxPresetColors` parameter logic. The guard condition has at least one known edge case defect (negative values) and several subtle boundary cases (`0`, `Infinity`, `NaN`, values equal to the exact preset count, values greater than the preset count). Given that `usePresets` is a local hook, consider either exporting it for direct testing or adding component-level tests that cover these inputs. At a minimum, `0` (no limit), `Infinity` (no limit), a boundary count, and a negative value should be exercised.

The JSDoc on `ColorConfig.maxPresetColors` documents two separate sentinel values (`0` and `Infinity`) that both mean "no limit." This dual-sentinel API is slightly inconsistent—one option is usually preferable. `0` is the more ergonomic choice for typical user configuration (no floating-point special values), so consider noting in the JSDoc that `Infinity` is accepted for convenience but `0` is the canonical way to express "no limit". Alternatively, you could normalize `Infinity` to `0` before the guard check to keep the internal logic to a single sentinel.
